tools.name: get_desk_messages
tools.description: Read the user's Desk messages: the handwritten line Sanduhr draws on the macOS desktop, picked from ~/Library/Application Support/Desk/messages.txt. Returns every raw line of the file (comments and effects included), whether one line is pinned, the rotation (daily or hourly), mix_daily (whether plain lines take turns with a weekday's own lines), today: the usual raw line the Desk shows now, and today_special: the date lines it shows above it today (empty on most days). Call this before propose_desk_messages to match the user's voice and to avoid repeats. messages.txt syntax, one line each: a plain line shows on any day; 'Mon: text' only on that weekday (Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun, exactly so); '10-31: text' only on that date (MM-DD); '# text' is a comment and blank lines are ignored. Each day the Desk shows one usual line: today's weekday lines if there are any (they replace the plain lines that day, unless the user's mix_daily switch is on, which lets the plain lines take turns with them), else the plain lines; it rotates through them once a day (a weekday's lines once a week) or once an hour (rotate, the user's choice), steady in between. Date lines are special days: they do not replace the usual line, they add to it, drawn above it, and every line for that date shows (two birthdays on one date both show; more than 3 take turns hourly, 3 at a time). So birthdays, anniversaries and holidays are date lines, one per person or occasion, short and friendly, like '03-14: {ink:#ff7e5f,#feb47b} happy birthday, Sam.'; the user's everyday line still shows under them. Pinning one line is a user setting (pinned): the pinned line replaces the usual line every day, so weekday and plain lines don't show while it is pinned (say so before proposing them), but date lines still stack above the pinned line, so birthdays and holidays show either way. The user's On special days setting (special_mode) decides how the date's lines share the Desk with the usual line: stack (all at once, the date's lines on top), turns (one at a time, crossfading) or scroll (one at a time, gliding up like a slow ticker), each line shown for special_seconds. Effects: tags at the start of the text, after any prefix, in any order, each in braces: {ink:#ff2a6d,#05d9e8} this line's ink, 1 to 4 hex colors (2 or more make a left-to-right gradient); {glow} / {noglow} turn the soft glow on or off for this line; {size:1.3} scales the line from 0.5 to 2 times the Desk's message size; {write} draws the line in, left to right like handwriting, once when it first appears; {shimmer} sends a slow light sweep across it every few seconds; {sweep} runs a three-character light across the line that brightens it toward white, once when the line appears, and {sweep:20} every 20 seconds (2 to 3600); {font:small-caps} draws the line in a letter style: bold, italic, bold-italic and small-caps in the Desk's own handwriting (its Bold face, a slant, capitals at x-height size), sans, mono, double-struck, script and fraktur as Unicode math letters (A to Z, a to z and, where the style has them, digits; accents and punctuation stay as written) in the system font. Examples: '{ink:#ffd08a} showtime.', 'Fri: {ink:#ff2a6d,#05d9e8} {glow} ship it.', '10-31: {ink:#ff7518,#6b2fa0} {write} happy halloween.', '{size:0.8} {noglow} breathe.', '{font:small-caps} {sweep} showtime.', '{font:script} {sweep:30} good morning.'. Good taste: short lines (handwriting reads best under about 40 characters, two lines at most on screen), lowercase and a period suit the hand, {write}, {shimmer} and {sweep} sparingly (a few lines, not every line, and one of them per line), {font:...} on short lines, gradients with 2 or 3 colors that sit near each other, sizes near 1. Reduce Motion shows {write} at once and skips {shimmer} and {sweep}.

tools.name: propose_desk_messages

lines.description: The lines, exactly as they would sit in messages.txt (prefix first, then effects, then the text).

mode.description: add appends the lines (lines already in the list are skipped); replace swaps the whole list for them (the comment block at the top of the file stays). Default add.

note.description: One short sentence for the user on why these lines (shown beside the suggestion).

tools.name: propose_theme
tools.description: Give the Sanduhr widget a new color theme. Call when the user asks for a theme, a new look, or colors from an image, a palette, or a vibe. The theme object uses the snake_case fields of docs/themes/template.json. Required: name (1 to 24 characters; the theme strip shows about 12, so keep it short and Title Case) and fourteen colors, each '#rrggbb' (a hash and six hex digits; no '#fff', no alpha): bg (window background, the darkest shade), glass (card fill), glass_on_mica (the card as it sits over the desktop's blur, usually a touch darker than glass), title_bg, footer_bg, border, bar_bg (the empty part of a bar), text, text_secondary, text_dim, text_muted (one hue, each darker than the last), accent (the brand color: the top strip, the readout's glow), sparkline (the history line, the accent's hue) and pace_marker (the tick that says where usage should be by now). Optional: description (one line, up to 200 characters, shown when the user hovers the theme in Settings; say what the look is), and the glass dials: glass_alpha (0 to 1, readable at 0.7 to 0.9), border_alpha (0 to 1, 0.2 to 0.6 is subtle), border_tint ('#rrggbb' in the accent's hue, or null for the plain border), accent_bloom ({blur: 0 to 20, alpha: 0 to 1}, 3 to 8 and 0.25 to 0.65 read well), inner_highlight ({color: '#rrggbb', alpha: 0.15 to 0.30} or null), card_corner_radius (0 to 24, default 10), breath_period_ms (500 to 20000, the bar's slow breathing, default 2800), ghost_alpha (0 to 1, the pace ghost tick), opts_out_of_mica (true makes the cards opaque; then set glass_alpha 1), monospace_font (any string gives monospaced numbers), and the title's text style: title_ink (2 to 4 '#rrggbb' colors, the widget title's gradient left to right; each stop needs 4.5:1 on the card like text) and title_style (its letters: bold, italic, bold-italic and small-caps in the widget font, sans, mono, double-struck, script and fraktur as Unicode letters), so a synthwave theme can carry its text too. What makes a good theme, measured by the lint: a dark base (bg, glass and glass_on_mica luminance under 0.25: light glass does not layer); text at 4.5:1 or better on the card (glass_on_mica at glass_alpha over a mid-gray desktop) and text_secondary at 3:1; the text ramp one hue at decreasing luminance; one accent hue shared by accent, sparkline and border_tint; a pace_marker distinct from the accent that stands out on the green bar fill (#4ade80) and on bar_bg by brightness (1.4:1) or by hue (60 degrees apart; a complementary hue works). The usage bars themselves stay green, yellow, orange and red. On the Mac the widget can also wear the built-in Match Desk theme (no glass, the Desk's own font and ink), and the Desk draws its meters in its own ink on the wallpaper beside the widget: a theme whose accent and text sit well next to the user's Desk ink reads as one desktop, and Match Desk itself cannot be replaced. A theme is checked here first: status rejected with findings (level, field, message) means fix the named fields and call again, nothing was written; warnings ride along with a theme that goes through. Then Sanduhr asks the user, who sees a preview card with the description and chooses Save, Save & Apply or Dismiss: pending_approval means the user decides (the result arrives later; do not propose the same theme again). When the user lets Claude change themes directly, Sanduhr saves it to its themes folder and applies it at once (apply: false saves without switching): applied or saved, with key, previous_key (the theme in use before, so the user can go back) and saved_path. A built-in's name (Obsidian, Aurora, Ember, Mint, 626 Labs, Matrix, Blueprint, Match Desk) is refused: pick another name or pass save_as. A theme whose key is taken by a different theme of the user's is saved under the next free key (ocean-2) and the result names renamed_from; the user's own theme is never overwritten. queued means Sanduhr did not answer: it is not running, and picks the request up within ten minutes. This server never writes a theme itself.

theme.description: The theme JSON: name, the fourteen #rrggbb colors, optional description and dials (docs/themes/template.json).

save_as.description: File key under the themes folder. Default: the name, slugged.

tools.name: propose_now_playing_looks
tools.description: Suggest a look for songs the user plays: a gradient and a letter style per song, drawn on the now playing line on the user's notch and Desk while Sanduhr's Style what's playing is on (Settings, Desk, Now Playing). Until a song has a look it wears one picked from its name out of eight palettes. Pass looks: 1 to 50 of {artist, title, colors, font, mood}: artist and title exactly as the player shows them (matched ignoring case and extra spaces), colors 2 to 4 hex colors left to right (each must read on the black notch: 3:1 or better against black, so no dark shades), font one letter style (bold, italic, bold-italic, small-caps drawn in the user's handwriting font; sans, mono, double-struck, script, fraktur as Unicode letters; omit for plain), mood up to 3 words for the user ('neon night drive'). Pick songs you know the user plays (they said so, or ask them); a look should feel like the song: its era, its cover, its energy. Sanduhr checks the looks again and, unless the user lets Claude style songs directly, shows them as a suggestion to Save or Dismiss: pending_approval means the user decides, applied means they are saved (looks_saved), rejected comes with reasons. style_on says whether Style what's playing is on; when it is false, tell the user where to switch it on. A saved look replaces an older one for the same song. queued means Sanduhr did not answer: it is not running. This server never writes the saved looks and never reads what is playing.

colors.description: 2 to 4 hex colors, left to right, each 3:1 or better on black.

tools.name: propose_widget
tools.description: Make a widget for the user's Sanduhr Desk with them: a pixel-art companion sprite, a palette pack for the Desk ink, or an effects pack. Call when the user asks for a desk pet, a companion, a sprite, a palette or an effect preset. The pack is data only: never a PNG, never a font, never code. A widget theme goes through propose_theme instead. Pass kind, pack {id, name (1-40), description (1-200), version?, author?, license?} and the kind's files. Sanduhr namespaces the id my-<id>, writes pack.json and a LICENSE (CC0-1.0 by default), validates the whole pack with the catalog's own rules (strict), and refuses with status rejected and reasons before anything is sent. Trademark rule: no 'claude' or 'anthropic' anywhere and no 'opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku' or 'fable' as words, in any name, description, author, file name or JSON string; original art only, no studio or game characters. SPRITE: sprite = sprite.json, schema_version 2: frame_w and frame_h (8 to 32 for pixel sheets), scale 1-4 (nearest neighbour), fps 1-24, either sheet (one .json path) or stages (1-6 of {id kebab 2-20, name 1-24, min_growth 0 for the first then strictly increasing up to 1, sheet, frame_w, frame_h}; stage 0's size equals the top-level size; stages grow with the user's coding days, never tokens), animations (name to 1-64 frame indexes; required: walk, sit, nap, pop, cheer, worry, focus, sleep, celebrate), moods {content, focused, worried, exhausted, celebrate} and triggers {needs_you, job_passed, near_limit, idle} each naming an animation, roam {edges: subset of bottom, left, right; speed_px_s 5-120}. sheets = path to a pixel sheet: {palette: 1-16 '#rrggbb' colors, never #ffffff (use #f0f0f0), frame_w, frame_h (equal to the stage's), frames: 1-256 frames, each exactly frame_h strings of exactly frame_w characters, top row first; '.' is transparent and 0-9, a-f (lowercase) index the palette}. Frame i is frames[i]; every sheet needs a frame for the highest index any animation uses. Keep the character on transparency, readable at scale 2, and give walk two or more frames. PALETTE: palettes = 1-64 of {name: lowercase-kebab 2-24, unique; colors: 1-4 '#rrggbb' stops left to right; mood? up to 24 characters}. EFFECTS: effects = 1-64 of {name as for palettes, type glow|sweep|shimmer|pulse, intensity 0-1, period_ms integer 400-10000, color '#rrggbb' or 'ink'}. Sanduhr checks the pack again and previews it on the Desk (a sprite as the companion, a palette as the Desk ink) with a review bar: previewing means the user is looking at it; it installs only when they press Apply (applied, as a local widget made here, listed in Settings, Widgets; companion true when they made a sprite the companion), and Dismiss answers rejected with reason dismissed and writes nothing. 'Let Claude change the Desk directly' does not cover widgets: a new pack always waits for Apply. queued means Sanduhr did not answer: it is not running. Nothing is uploaded; sharing a pack is a pull request to the sanduhr-widgets catalog.

kind.description: What the pack is. A widget theme goes through propose_theme instead; fonts are never proposed.

pack.description: pack.json's own fields. Sanduhr writes files, kind, schema_version and sanduhr_min, and the LICENSE text.

id.description: Lowercase kebab-case; Sanduhr prefixes my- (3 to 40 characters with it).

author.description: Default: Made here. Never a brand or model name.

license.description: Default CC0-1.0. Sanduhr writes the matching LICENSE.

sprite.description: kind sprite: sprite.json (schema_version 2): frame_w, frame_h, scale, fps, sheet or stages, animations, moods, triggers, roam. Every sheet path ends .json and is a key of sheets.

sheets.description: kind sprite: pixel sheets, path (such as sheet.json or sprites/egg.json) to {palette, frame_w, frame_h, frames}.

palettes.description: kind palette: palettes.json, {schema_version: 1, palettes: [...]} or the list alone.

effects.description: kind effects: effects.json, {schema_version: 1, effects: [...]} or the list alone.

note.description: One short sentence for the user on what you made and why (shown on the review bar).

tools.name: get_desk
tools.description: Read the user's Desk before designing it. The Desk is what Sanduhr draws on the Mac desktop: a clock, Claude usage, a handwritten message and other pieces, each placed at one of eight anchors (tl tc tr ml mr bl bc br) with a size, in a font and an ink, optionally on a soft plate. Returns design (the current look as a design: layout with every piece's anchor, size, hidden and tilt (the slant of its stack in degrees, 0 upright), and for claude, meters and telemetry its style (bar, slim, ring or ticks; limits.piece_style lists the pieces and the words), weather.nickname (the name the weather piece shows instead of the place's, "" for the place's own), font, ink, plate, shadow), pieces and anchors (the allowed words), fonts (installed families, and the bundled handwriting fonts EsteFont Pro and EsteFont 26), shown (the pieces the Desk draws now), message_color and notch_text_color (hex colors, read-only: propose_desk does not change them), limits and sprites (each sprite made here: id, name, frame_w, frame_h and cells, never its image; propose_sprite_motion uses it). The Mac Desk has no monitors, wallpaper summary, Launcher, saved designs or direct-change switch, so those keys are never here, and propose_desk cannot judge ink against the wallpaper: choose an ink that reads on what the user has. Call this before propose_desk and design from what it says. status no_data with reason missing means Sanduhr is not running or has not written the Desk state yet.

tools.name: propose_desk
tools.description: Propose a look for the user's Desk. The design is PARTIAL: send only the fields to change; everything absent stays as it is. Fields, all optional: name (up to 40 characters); note (one sentence for the user, up to 200); layout {piece: {anchor, size, hidden}}, where piece is a key from get_desk pieces, anchor is tl tc tr ml mr bl bc br, size is 0.6 to 1.6, and hidden removes the piece (the companion piece draws the sprite the user chose in Settings, Widgets, and draws nothing until a sprite is installed); tilt in a layout piece slants the piece's whole stack from -20 to 20 degrees (negative rises to the right, positive falls; 0 upright), so a left stack at -18 and a right stack at 18 read as two faces of a fold; pieces at one anchor share one slant, so give them the same tilt; style in a layout piece, only on claude, meters and telemetry, is how its numbers draw so a stack fits its column: bar (the default, a full-width bar with its label above), slim (label and value on one line over a thin bar, about half the height; claude becomes a compact two-row line), ring (small arc gauges with the value inside, side by side in a row), ticks (ten segmented cells, the OLED-friendly one); a Claude limit keeps its pace mark in every style; font (a family from get_desk fonts.installed or the bundled EsteFont Pro or EsteFont 26, or {family, link} with an https link to get a font the user lacks: Sanduhr never downloads it, the review shows the link and Apply waits for the font, status needs_font); ink (one #rrggbb, or a list of 2 to 4 #rrggbb for a left-to-right gradient); plate and shadow (true or false; the plate is a soft panel behind each stack of pieces); weather {nickname} (up to 24 characters, shown on the Desk's weather piece instead of the place's name, "" for the place's own name; the city and the unit stay the user's to choose in Settings, Weather). The Mac refuses, with a reason and nothing written, what only Windows has: monitor in a layout piece, the launcher and glow pieces, the launcher field, the messages, looks and theme fields (send message lines with propose_desk_messages, song looks with propose_now_playing_looks and a widget theme with propose_theme), and the Windows ink words auto, light, dark and theme. The server checks before anything is sent: every field's shape and range, the tilt of each stack and the style words. status rejected comes with reasons, each {field, message}: fix those fields and call again; nothing was written. Otherwise Sanduhr draws the design live on the desktop with a bar on Settings, Desk where the user chooses Apply or Dismiss: previewing means the user is reviewing it now (do not send the same look again), applied means it is in place (their previous look is saved), needs_font lists the fonts (family, link) the user must install first, queued means Sanduhr did not answer and will show it when it starts. A whole design always waits for the user's Apply: the switch that lets Claude change Desk messages directly does not cover it. This server never changes the Desk itself.

design.description: A partial Desk design: only the fields to change. See the tool description for each field.

layout.description: Piece key (from get_desk pieces) to {anchor: tl|tc|tr|ml|mr|bl|bc|br, size: 0.6-1.6, hidden: boolean, tilt: -20 to 20 degrees, the slant of the piece's whole stack, style: bar|slim|ring|ticks, only on claude, meters and telemetry}. monitor is Windows only and refused here.

weather.description: {nickname: up to 24 characters}: the name the weather piece shows instead of the place's own; "" goes back to the place's name. Local only; the forecast keeps the city's coordinates.

font.description: A font family name, or {family, link} with an https link to get a font the user lacks.

ink.description: One #rrggbb color, or a list of 2 to 4 #rrggbb colors (gradient). The Windows words auto, light, dark and theme are refused here.

launcher.description: Windows only: refused here with a reason.

messages.description: Not part of a Mac design: refused here with a reason (use propose_desk_messages).

looks.description: Not part of a Mac design: refused here with a reason (use propose_now_playing_looks).

theme.description: Not part of a Mac design: refused here with a reason (use propose_theme).

note.description: One short sentence for the user on why this look (shown in the review bar; overrides design.note).
